t.5.25.1: Thus harshly addressed by Sītā, the rākṣasīs were overcome with rage, and some of them went to report it to the mighty Rāvaṇa.
t.5.25.2: Then the rākṣasīs of dreadful appearance approached Sītā and once more spoke to her harsh words, all of one purport, aimed at her harm.
t.5.25.3: Now then, ignoble Sītā, you of wicked resolve, the rākṣasīs will devour this flesh of yours at their pleasure.
t.5.25.4: Then, seeing Sītā threatened by those ignoble women, the aged rākṣasī Trijaṭā, who was lying down, spoke these words.
t.5.25.5: Devour yourselves, you ignoble ones! You shall not eat Sītā, the beloved daughter of Janaka and the daughter-in-law of Daśaratha.
t.5.25.6: For today I have seen a dream, dreadful and hair-raising, which foretells the destruction of the rākṣasas and the prosperity of this woman's husband.
t.5.25.7: Thus addressed by Trijaṭā, the rākṣasīs, though overcome with anger, all became frightened and spoke these words to Trijaṭā.
t.5.25.8: Tell us: what kind of dream is this that you have seen in the night?
t.5.25.9: Having heard the words that issued from the mouths of those rākṣasīs, Trijaṭā then spoke at that moment words concerning a dream.
t.5.25.10: Rāghava himself, having mounted a divine palanquin made of ivory, yoked to a thousand horses and travelling through the sky,
t.5.25.11: And today in a dream I saw Sītā, clad in white garments, standing upon a white mountain encircled by the ocean; Sītā was united with Rāma, as radiance is with the sun.
t.5.25.12: And Rāghava was seen by me, mounted on a great four-tusked elephant resembling a mountain; together with Lakṣmaṇa he roamed about.
t.5.25.13: Then those two tigers among men, blazing with their own splendour and wearing white garlands and garments, came and stood beside Jānakī.
t.5.25.15: Then the lotus-eyed one was seen by me, having sprung up from her husband's lap, stroking the moon and the sun with her two hands.
t.5.25.14: Then, on the summit of that mountain, Jānakī mounted the shoulder of the elephant standing in the sky, the elephant held by her husband.
t.5.25.16: Then that finest of elephants, mounted by those two princes and by wide-eyed Sītā, stood above Laṅkā.
t.5.25.17: He himself, wearing white garlands and garments, came in a chariot yoked with eight white bulls, accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa, together with Lakṣmaṇa his brother and with Sītā his wife.
t.5.25.18: Today Rāvaṇa, fallen to the ground from the aerial chariot Puṣpaka, was seen being dragged by a woman, shaven-headed and clad once more in black garments.
t.5.25.20: A dark woman clad in red, her limbs smeared with mud, has bound Daśagrīva by the neck and drags him toward the southern quarter, the direction of Yama.
t.5.25.19: Wearing red garlands and red unguents, he set out toward the southern quarter in a chariot yoked with donkeys and entered a muddy lake.
t.5.25.21: Daśagrīva on a boar, Indrajit on a porpoise, and Kumbhakarṇa on a camel set out toward the southern direction.
t.5.25.22: And a great gathering took place, resounding with the sound of songs and musical instruments, of rākṣasas wearing red garlands and red garments, who were drinking.
t.5.25.23: And this delightful city of Laṅkā, crowded with horses and chariots, was seen fallen into the ocean, its gate-towers and archways shattered.
t.5.25.24: Having drunk oil, all the rākṣasa women, dancing wildly and laughing with loud cries, were seen in Laṅkā, which had become rough with ashes.
t.5.25.25: And all these bulls among the rākṣasas, Kumbhakarṇa and the others, having put on red garments, have entered a lake of cow dung.
t.5.25.26: Go away, be gone! Rāghava is winning back Sītā. In his supreme wrath he would surely slay you together with all the rākṣasas.
t.5.25.27: Rāghava will not tolerate that his beloved, highly esteemed wife, who followed him faithfully into life in the forest, should be reviled or even threatened.
t.5.25.28: Therefore enough of your cruel words; let only gentle words be spoken. Let us entreat Vaidehī, for this is what pleases me.
t.5.25.29: For the sorrowing woman to whom such a dream appears is freed from her many sorrows and attains an unsurpassed joy.
t.5.25.31: For Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka, is pleased by prostration; O rākṣasīs, she is able to rescue you from great danger.
t.5.25.30: Though you have threatened her, O rākṣasīs, now entreat her; what use is this eagerness to talk? For a terrible danger from Rāghava has come upon the rākṣasas.
t.5.25.32: Moreover, on the limbs of this large-eyed lady I do not perceive any adverse mark, not even a very subtle one.
t.5.25.34: But I see that the fulfilment of Vaidehī's purpose is at hand, as are the destruction of the lord of the rākṣasas and the victory of Rāghava.
t.5.25.33: But I suspect that the sorrow which has come upon her is merely a flaw of the shadow, for this queen, who does not deserve sorrow, has been seen standing in the sky.
t.5.25.35: This has become an omen that she will hear something greatly pleasing, for her eye, long like a lotus petal, is seen to throb.
t.5.25.37: And her peerless left thigh, like the trunk of an elephant, trembling, seems to announce that Rāghava stands before her.
t.5.25.36: And one arm of this gracious Vaidehī, the left one, slightly thrilled with bristling hair, suddenly trembles without any cause.
t.5.25.38: And a bird that has entered its nest among the branches, again and again speaking the most soothing words and uttering a voice of happy welcome, rises up again and again as though delighted.
